(Adding Message Walls) by Toa Kopaka Nuva[]

This was previously done here but as there were some unknowns in regrards to how it would be in a new fandom update I thought it would be fair to run it again.

Here is what I see as the pros

  1. Conversations are in one place. No more having to jump to different talk pages.
  2. It is the same format as discussions making it easier for all users.

Here are what a see as the cons

  1. As far as I know threads can be deleted from a users message wall by them and can only be seen by an admin.

Current talk pages would be archived and would still be able to be read.

Support

  1. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 19:39, 1 January 2022 (UTC)
  2. TitaniumNinja74 (talk) 21:29, 1 January 2022 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. I feel like talk pages are overall easier to use than message walls, and templates like the Warning template cannot be used, as from my experience, the templates do not preview. It is also useful to have users remove messages in case of troll or any harm or disruptive behavior.   LuigiMaster41   Talk 20:21, 1 January 2022 (UTC)
  2. This would be a very good idea before the migration to the UCP. But things have changed. Now message walls are separated from MediaWiki and thus, they no longer support its convenient syntax, templates, etc. I think that "having to jump to different talk pages" is much better than having to lose all those features. Person from Ninjago \ 20:51, 1 January 2022 (UTC)
  3. The post UCP message walls are even worse than the pre-UCP ones. There is no talk page archive anymore, it is completely impossible to look at the messages from before message walls. Also, what I said in the previous vote about old messages being hard to find still stands but it is even worse now because at least before there was a way to quickly get to your oldest messages.Ninja72 (talk) 21:40, 1 January 2022 (UTC)
  4. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 08:18, 2 January 2022 (UTC)

Neutral

Comments

The result of the vote was: Oppose


(Galleries change) by Legoninjagofan600[]

Here are my two ideas of changing the galleries:

1) Galleries would be sorted chronologically. I don't mean that flashbacks should be the first and the like, but rather this. For example, in Wu's gallery, all canon-installments are placed on the top and the others, non-canon-like Wu's Teas are at the bottom (just those connected to the show, not for example video games). I think they should be placed where they take place or when they were released, because it looks like Wu's Teas are the latest shorts and they are 5 years old.

2) Concept art location. Some user (I don't remember who) has placed all the concept art at the very bottom of the classic galleries on the pages, but someone who doesn't know about it will never find them there due to the often very long galleries. Therefore, I think they should be placed on top, right after the promotional media section.

What do you think about these things?

Galleries would be sorted chronologically

Support

  1.   LuigiMaster41   Talk 12:12, 5 January 2022 (UTC)
  2. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 16:15, 5 January 2022 (UTC)
  3. Ninja72 (talk) 18:44, 5 January 2022 (UTC)
  4. I think it is best to use the same order as in the Appearances section. Person from Ninjago \ 18:50, 5 January 2022 (UTC)

Neutral

(Appearances section on episode pages) by Wikifan988[]

I propose that we combine the Locations and Non-speaking characters sections, along with a number of new sections, into an Appearances section on episode pages that has several subsections. Like on the Marvel Cinematic Universe Wiki, the other sections would include Events, Items, Creatures, Vehicles, and Mentioned, the last of which would be for characters who were only mentioned in the episode (alternatively, we could have a section called Characters that would be divided into three sections: Speaking, Non-speaking, and Mentioned). Events/Items/Creatures/Vehicles that are only mentioned would be listed in their respective sections, with (mentioned) next to them. Also, I'm not sure what would be the best order to list these different sections, though alphabetical order may be fine. Let me know what you think.

Edit: Also a Species section.

Support

  1. Samurai viper (talk) 01:43, 6 January 2022 (UTC)
  2. I think it's a very good idea and I agree with that. It will be a lot of work, but I think it could be done. PS: You can vote for your own proposal. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 08:01, 6 January 2022 (UTC)
  3. Good idea!   LuigiMaster41   Talk 16:00, 6 January 2022 (UTC)
  4. Agreed with Ninja. I think the following is the best order: Events, Places, Characters (Speaking and Non-speaking), Creatures, Vehicles, and Objects, not Items. Person from Ninjago \ 16:05, 6 January 2022 (UTC)
  5. Wikifan988 (talk) 23:17, 6 January 2022 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

Comments

For speaking characters, there are already the cast sections, so if we go with the Characters section that is divided into three sections, then the Speaking characters section should just include the actors next to the characters like we do now and replace the Cast section, because otherwise, it is basically duplication.Ninja72 (talk) 11:30, 6 January 2022 (UTC)

@Legoninjagofan Thanks for the reminder.

@Person from Ninjago Good point about Objects, that would be more consistent. Though thinking about it more, since I feel that speaking characters would still be the most looked-for/important section, Characters should be first which would make alphabetical order the most logical option.

@Ninja72 That would make sense, though I have a question: if a character appeared in a flashback only, would it say (flashback) next to the character's name like it would in the other sections like for Locations that only appeared in flashback? For example, "Garmadon (flashback) - Mark Oliver". The problem is that I feel this would be rather awkward and would be mixing in-universe and out-of-universe too much. I also have some other ideas for how Cast/Speaking characters sections could be done but I don't know if I should get into that now since this proposal is already pretty big. Wikifan988 (talk) 23:17, 6 January 2022 (UTC)

That is a good point, alphabetical order is better. Good idea about characters that only appeared in flashbacks, but I think that would be good to have the word "flashback" in brackets and the Mentioned subsection in other sections too. Person from Ninjago \ 23:57, 6 January 2022 (UTC)

This Characters + Cast section thing is used on Scoobypedia, where the Characters and Cast sections are separate and I don't think that's a big deal to do it that way. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 07:30, 7 January 2022 (UTC)

I still think it would be unnecessarily repeating information. Maybe only have Non-speaking and mentioned characters as sub-headings of appearances and then leave the Cast section as the place that lists speaking characters.Ninja72 (talk) 09:50, 7 January 2022 (UTC)

I agree with Legoninjagofan, but since I didn't specify in my proposal and referenced the MCU Wiki which does not include speaking characters in its Appearances section, and also because having both a Cast and Characters section could involve reorganizing how the way we do the Cast section, let's go with Ninja72's suggestion for now and I will make another vote for the Cast/Characters thing at a later point. Wikifan988 (talk) 22:39, 7 January 2022 (UTC)

The result of the vote was: Support


(Change Explorers Club back to Explorer's Club) by Samurai viper[]

The reason for proposing this vote is that after looking at the Explorers Club article, I think we should rename it back to Explorer's Club.

Reasons:

  1. The article was originally called that before it was changed to the one we have now.
  2. Most of the episodes that show or mentioned the club named the building as the "Explorer's Club" and not "Explorers Club" in their synopses.
  3. Sites that list the episode also labels the name as "Explorer's Club". Examples: Cartoon Network, Sky.com, and the LEGO channel on YouTube.
  4. Certain episodes are known for having an error for their title cards such as misspells, punctuations, or adding an extra word.

So, unless there's a source (other than the title for Episode 111) that names as the club as the "Explorers Club", I think we should rename the articles back to the way it was before, "Explorer's Club" for the building and "The Explorer's Club" for the episode.

Location

(Change the Quote template back) by Person from Ninjago[]

I think that the {{Quote}} template should be changed back, here are the reasons:

  • The current version of the template only allows for one character's line, whereas the previous version allowed for multiple characters' statements;
  • Its design seems inconsistent with most of the infoboxes. This can be fixed by modifying the latter, but I think that their current design is really great and I am afraid that it might get worse.

However, since one of the main reasons for the previous change was that the color mix might look bad with the dark or light theme or the text could not be seen at all, I suggest that we can change text color variants to black and white only, as one of them would always match the main color with both themes. Another option is to somehow modify the current template to allow for multiple characters' lines, but with the quote and infobox inconsistency persistent.

(Update the infobox design) by LuigiMaster41[]

So this is a proposal originally made by Wikifan988 and was allowed to be brought back by Toa Kopaka Nuva.

Basically, what the proposal is asking is to update the infoboxes likes the ones for Characters, Objects, Elements, etc. to more modern infobox styles, like the Avatar Wiki for an example. (Deal with the "tabber situation" in infoboxes) by Samurai viper[]

This may be unnoticeable to users, but there's kinda a problem with the tabbers. Users often argue of which images should be used in the infoboxes to form a tabber or not. And some of are only added or removed because of fairness or how prominent it was in the storyline.

  1. Examples:
    1. Clouse and Wu had their young and cyborg appearances in their infoboxes for years since it was introduced until it was removed. And want to know why? It was because Chen and Cyrus Borg didn't have that in their respective infobox, and it took years for it to be pointed out.
    2. Legoninjagofan600 tried to add a tabber for Vania just because we did one for Harumi and make it fair, but a year later, he added a tabber for the Iron Doom about it being intact and destroyed, but didn't do the same thing with the other vehicles that are currently destroyed or heavily damaged, which was why the tabber got removed.
  2. Last year, Joker1943 tried to add a tabber for Skales and his appearance as a General and a Warrior, but it got taken down because Skales is a major character and his appearance as a warrior was only in two episodes. But what does this mean for Wu (who is a major character) and his appearance as the "Dragon Master", which also only appeared in two episodes (not counting the Ninjago history mural)? Or P.I.X.A.L., who is also a major character and only have her Season 7 Samurai X suit appeared in two episodes.
    1. Honestly, doesn't the fact that the Season 7 Samurai X suit image is used for P.I.X.A.L.'s tabber mean that we used 3/4 of the images for the infobox? And two of them are about her being Samurai X?

So after looking at these past edits, I think we should do one of these suggestions.

  1. Users now have to make a vote about adding, replacing, or removing an image in a tabber for the characters, objects, etc. Similar to how we now have to make a vote of replacing an infobox image unless it's in higher quality.
  2. Add a requirement section in the Manual of Style, where it would say how images are able to be necessary to be used for a tabber, such as a drastic appearance/change that appeared in more than two episodes.

Users now have to propose a vote for tabbers in infoboxes

(Add Imageref template) by Wikifan988[]

When users who do not have fandom accounts or who are not signed in click on image references (such as the ones see here - try clicking on one besides the first one when signed out), it automatically redirects to one of the pages that the image is on, unless no pages feature the image. This makes it difficult and inconvenient for these readers, who will most often not be able to discern the relevant image within a gallery of other images. However, thanks to Mr Pie 5's help, I was able to create a template that would solve this problem. As seen here, the {{Imageref}} template would allow for linking images in such a way that the specific image would always appear for the user instead of redirecting to another page with several images.

Support

  1. No reason to oppose. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 19:58, 28 January 2022 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

Comments

The result of the vote was: Support


(Change quote template) by Printer89[]

So we've been trying to create the perfect quote template - from the ability to change the color of the quotation marks, background color, and text color, to the shape of template, the ability to have multiple lines, and something compatible to dark theme. However, it's impossible to satisfy every single thing on the list. There have been some complaints about our current template which is why I'm suggesting we change to this template and get rid of the dialogue template. I think this template is our best option because it resembles our very first quote template minus the border. Our first template had the ability to have multiple lines, so we get that feature back without an additional template. However, users won't have the ability to change the quotation marks, text color, and background color so it may be seen as a drawback, but given the fact we have a dark theme to manage, the colors will work for one theme but not for another. Meanwhile, this template is perfect for both theme because the text color will automatically change depending on the theme. While it may look plain, I think being simple is the best option going forward if we are to check most of the boxes.

(Replace the "affiliations" field in infoboxes with a subsection for affiliations and enemies) by Samurai viper[]

Recently, there's been a problem with the affiliations for the infoboxes. At one hand, it's okay, but on the other hand it's a bit of an… overuse.

Take Wu's infobox for example. I mean, if we include the Munce and Geckles in his affiliation, then that means we also have to include the Order of Felis, the villagers from The Lair of Tanabrax, the Ninjago City Police, the Ninja Replacements, etc. Because Wu was affiliated with all of those groups as well (and was affiliated with the Order of Felis way longer compared to the Munce and Geckles). But, including those group, will overcrowd Wu's infobox. The same will go for each of the ninja if we include all the groups they worked with.

Look at Steve Rogers' infobox in the MCU Wiki. His affiliation field doesn't list all the groups he worked with, just the ones he's a member of. We actually did this with most of the characters in the Ninjago Wiki, take a look at Jay's infobox for example.

So, I think we should actually have a section that would list all of the characters/creatures/groups' affiliations and enemies. Like how the MCU Wiki does it. Except, it will be listed by groups. Individuals will only be included if said individual isn't part of a specific group or the character only interacted with one member of a team.


This is an example of what Unagami's would be like.

Affiliations and enemies

Family

  • Milton Dyer - Creator/"Father"
  • Okino - Creation/"Son"

Allies

  • Red Visors - Formerly
  • Sushimi's kitchen staff - Formerly
  • Avatar Harumi - Formerly
  • Red aerial drones - Formerly
  • Whack Rats - Formerly
  • The Mechanic - Formerly
  • Kryptarium inmates - Formerly

Enemies

  • Ninja - Formerly
  • Scott - Formerly
  • Henchmen - Former allies

And this would be Vangelis'

Affiliations and enemies

Family

  • Vania - Daughter

Allies

  • Hazza D'ur
  • Re-Awakened
  • Grief-Bringer

Enemies

  • Army of Shintaro - Former subordinates
  • Upply
  • Geckles
  • Munce
  • Ninja

And here are all my suggestions.

  • First suggestion: Add a section for all the character's affiliations and enemies, and have it replace the affiliations field in the infoboxes for characters, creatures, and groups.
  • Second suggestion: The affiliations field would only include the groups the character's a part of or be a major ally.
  • Third suggestion: Add a section for all the character's affiliations and enemies, and keep the affiliations field, but it can only include the groups the character (and creature) is a part of and/or be a major ally of said group.

First suggestion

Support

Oppose

Neutral

Second suggestion

Support

(Use "unnamed" descriptors in some character intros to avoid redundancy) by Wikifan988[]

I propose that in intro descriptions for some pages for characters without confirmed names, instead of having intros like the one on Ronin's wife's page, "Ronin's wife is the wife of Ronin," it would say, "An unnamed woman is the wife of Ronin." This makes it less redundant and awkward and prevents editors from having to find ways to repeat the same statement multiple times in a sentence. I was inspired to make this proposal after I created the page for Clancee's mother, because I had to write a somewhat awkward intro description to avoid repetition when I believe it would be better to just say "An unnamed Serpentine is Clancee's mother." Another example would be Grimfax's advisor, whose intro I would change from, "Grimfax's advisor was the royal advisor of Grimfax before Zane took over the Never-Realm," to, "An unnamed man was the royal advisor of Grimfax before Zane took over the Never-Realm." In other cases, like the Prune juice salesman, we could rearrange the description a bit so that instead of "The prune juice salesman is a salesman who sells prune juice in Ninjago City," it would say, "An unnamed man is a prune juice salesman in Ninjago City." Other pages such as Cole's grandfather and Jay's mother could go either way, so let me know what you think.

(Remove one of the voting rules) by Printer89[]

So after a vote which allowed users to vote on their own proposals, this rule which was never discussed was added:

If you are the only person to have voted on your proposal, then the proposal is counted as a tie and the rule about tied votes is applied.

I think this rule has too many problems and hasn't be thought out. Firstly, it gives too much power to an admin. Let's say the owner of the proposal is the only one to vote and it goes to deadlock. An admin can single handedly strike down the proposal although it should be tied since they have one vote. But in this case, it's like having two votes.

Secondly, it seems ridiculous if the owner of the proposal is the only one who voted, it goes to tiebreakers. But if a user who's not the creator of the proposal is the only one to vote, the proposal passes? There's no consistency whatsoever as in both cases, one person decides the outcome with the only difference being who's the one voting. I find it hard to pretend if a non owner user is the only one who voted, it's considered acceptable, but if the owner of the vote is the only one who voted, it's considered unacceptable.

Similarly, what are we suppose to do if the owner of the proposal has a stance while everyone else voted neutral? According to the rules, the proposal should pass since it states "If you are the only person..." but the truth is, whether you vote neutral or don't vote at all, they're pretty much the same thing with the only difference being whether you write your name down.

With that being said, I think the rule that was added in response of allowing users to vote on their own proposals should be removed. If users really cared about an issue, they would take a stance. But by not voting or voting neutral, users are basically saying "I don't care about the outcome" or they don't want to take sides.

Support

  1.   LuigiMaster41   Talk 20:14, 23 April 2022 (UTC)
  2. Samurai viper (talk) 00:50, 26 April 2022 (UTC)

Oppose

Neutral

(Deal with "transformations and alternative versions articles") by Samurai viper[]

Before anyone jumps to conclusions, no, I'm not saying we should make pages for characters' aliases such as Superstar Rockin' Jay or Heavy Metal. It's unnecessary to make pages for personas such as those because all they do is just change the design, not have a drastic change like how the Nunchucks of Lightning can transform into the Storm Glider.

We are actually known for making pages about transformations, but at the same, we're unaware of which ones. For example, the Black Bounty used to have a page, and we were okay with it until we merged it with the Destiny's Bounty just because it just was an "evil version" of the ship. Meanwhile, we're still okay with the evil versions of the Energy Dragon and Samurai Mech having their own pages.

Speaking of those two, was the reason that Morro's dragon has a page of its own because some sources describe the dragon to be the "Elemental Wind Dragon" despite it actually being another version of the Energy Dragon? If not, then what's the reason? The same goes with the Mech-enstein. What was the strongest reason an evil version of a mech is able to get a page of its own?

So, to prevent any confusion and unfairness in the future regarding transformations, I think we should vote on which alternate versions should have a page and which shouldn't.

Make pages for transformations with the same aspects

Normally, I don't think transformations that have the same aspects should have their own page unless it's a specific one. Like how the Kai Fighter is just one jet fighter, and they're still more of the original version. But at the same time, (apparently) I can be okay with it since some users are.

However, if this vote passes and someone wants to make a page for the transformations with the same aspects that don't have one, I think it should still be discussed first or approved by staff before actually being made into a page to prevent any complications. For example, if someone thinks that we should make a page for the Overlord Dragon, then that means they're requesting to make a page that will mostly be about a possession. Since the whole Overlord Dragon metamorphosis in Season 2 did happen because of a possession. Just like how the "Evil Green Ninja" happened because Morro possessed Lloyd.

On the other hand, transformations such as the Jungle Raider can immediately have a page of their own, as I mentioned before about the Kai Fighter. The same goes for vehicles such as the Chain Cycle and the Rattlercopter, as the original versions of those vehicles were generic ones, didn't have a name, and no significant role.

Examples
  • Destiny's Bounty -> Black Bounty
  • Samurai Mech -> Mech-enstein -> Samurai X Mech (P.I.X.A.L.)
  • Ultra Sonic Raider -> Ultra Stealth Raider

Support

Oppose

  1. Ninja72 (talk) 11:35, 30 April 2022 (UTC)

Make pages for transformations with different aspects

Pretty sure we can all agree that if the transformation has different aspects, then both versions should have separate pages. Especially if the transformation can be changed back and forth, like how the Golden Weapons and can turn into Elemental vehicles then back to weapons.

Basically, if a character's scepter can transform into a dragon and vice versa, then they should be in separate pages. The same thing goes if someone's castle can transform into a rocket, or if two robots can turn into giant mechs.

And to tell if the transformation has different aspects, you just need to look if it has different navigation boxes and/or other categories. Just like how each respective Golden Weapon and Elemental vehicle have different categories and navigation boxes. This will also be included for locations with different aspects. Since we did it with Garmadon's monastery (a monastery that was used to previously used by Garmadon to teach his students) and Steep Wisdom (a tea shop used by Wu to sell tea).

(Extending the time for a user to gain rights) by Legoninjagofan600[]

I was led to this idea by recent votes for Discussions Moderators, with most of the users who applied for the rights being on the wiki for a very short time. Currently, the user has to be on the wiki for 3 months (Rollback and Discussions Moderator), 5 months (Content Moderator), 8 months (Admin) and 1 year and 4 months (Bureaucrat). I suggest that this time be extended for Rollback Discussions Moderator and Content Moderator to 1 year and for Admin and Bureaucrat to 2 years. This may seem extreme to some, but for example when I first applied for rollback rights and was on the wiki for 1 year, I was told I should wait. I agree with that and I don't think it's a good idea to apply for rights 3 months after joining the wiki. A good example is the recent vote (I don't remember who the user was) for the Discussions Moderator, with a number of their friends (probably) going to vote for them, and they were only on the wiki for 2 weeks. Although the vote was canceled because it did not meet the 3-month condition, I still think that this condition should be extended. Also, gaining rights is na big thing and the user should earn them by being active on the wiki for a long time.

(Merge the Sons of Garmadon and the Red Crows) by Samurai viper[]

The reason for suggesting that we should merge the two groups, is because after reading the second issue, I learned that the Red Crows are actually the Sons of Garmadon, not a complete different group that Ultra Violet joined.

It all makes sense now if you look closely.

  1. After the ending of Issue 2, I believe one of the commentaries said, “We're happy to have you here, even if we're currently being overrun by Mogra and his Red Crows! But don't worry-Garmadon is on his way back and will react very strongly to these interlopers. The Sons of Garmadon may very well wish that they kept their original name!”
  2. The official description of the third issue said, "Garmadon has been the most evil person in Ninjago for a very, very long time, but his ALL NEW enemy has stolen his most loyal followers and…one of his most prized possessions?"
  3. In Issue 1, Mogra said, “The Sons of Garmadon ride no longer-- but the Red Crows shall fly forever!” after he asked Ultra Violet if she's still loyal to Garmadon.

All those notes show that Mogra just rebranded the Sons of Garmadon.

In addition, the members still have their SOG designs in all of the WildBrain installments they appear in. Despite Garmadon taking place after Season 10 (in other words, taking place during the WildBrain era), and the members having different designs (even though the designs between the two are the same but with different coloring and logo). Not sure if that's because of the "budget thing" or they decided to do the same thing as they did with the Sky Pirates.

So these are my reasons why we should merge the two pages:

  1. They're the same group. And separating the Sons of Garmadon and the Red Crows would be like separating Darkley's Boarding School and Wu's Academy, and Ninjago City and New Ninjago City.
  2. The members are still portrayed as the SOG in the show. Again not sure if that's because of the whole budget thing or the same reason for the Sky Pirates' absent.

Support

  2. Ninja72 (talk) 18:39, 19 May 2022 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. I'm not exactly sure how this idea would work with merging the two groups in one page, especially considering the fact that a possible factor for using SoG members could be due to "budget reasons". Remember that we have the ninja and Stranded ninja being separate pages despite having some of the same members in the latter group, and I believe there may have been a vote to merge the two pages together but was opposed, so I'm honestly unsure with how this would turn out.   LuigiMaster41   Talk 18:27, 19 May 2022 (UTC)
  2. Although the Red Crows originated from the Sons of Garmadon, I don't think the pages should be merged. This is because the groups have a completely different name, leader and goal, as the goal of the Sons of Garmadon was to revive Garmadon and subsequently serve him. Just because the Red Crows are made up of the Sons of Garmadon doesn't mean it's the same group. It would also be a problem to rename the page, because if they are known as "Red Crows" at the end of the comic, the page should be called that (since it's their recent name), but "Sons of Garmadon" is a much better known name, as not everyone reads the comics. (Change Image policy) by Legoninjagofan600[]

Although the name may be too general, I will try to explain everything in detail here. The problem I would like to solve is the policy of images from teasers from the official LEGO YouTube channel. Under current rules, these images can be uploaded to the wiki, but can only be found on the Season 15: Crystalized page. However, if a character, object location, or vehicle appears for the first time in the season and a page is created for it, a new image from the teaser can be inserted into the infobox. However, other images can't be added to the gallery of the page. This approach seems very illogical to me and I suggest that we be able to add images to all pages as soon as the teaser/trailer/scene is published. The images come from as official an source as they can, and although they only come from a teaser and someone might say they reveal the plot, I don't think that's a problem. LEGO publishes these scenes in order to attract people to the season. And we practically prevent this by not using new images. If LEGO has decided that these scenes will be published, then I do not see a problem considering them as spoilers here on the wiki. Finally, I would just like to add that this would only apply to images from the LEGO YouTube channel (or LEGO.com), not various leaks and the like, which of course would not be allowed.

PS: Images in infoboxes for characters who will not appear for the first time this season (such as Pythor or Skylor, or even the ninja) will remain the same until the release of the season, as we do not know the sequence of their design variants in this season and we always use the recent outfit.

(Overturn image exception vote, reduce voting time for images) by Printer89[]

This vote was allowed by Toa Kopaka Nuva to be brought back.

In the vote proposal, the result came out which was that all flashback images would not require a vote if a user was replacing a flashback image with a new image. However, for all other images if a user wanted to replace that image, it would require a vote.

It really doesn't make sense that a user can change a flashback image to whatever image they want without the community approving of that new image. We're basically relying on the fact the user who replaces the flashback gets it right the first time and picks hopefully the best image. And let's say someone doesn't like whoever replaced the flashback image. According to the rules, they would need to make a vote while the person who replaced the flashback doesn't need a vote. In some ways, this exception will only make the process more tedious and longer than if a vote were to take place right away. I'm fine with prioritizing actual images over flashbacks; I just think there should be a vote to decide what image takes its place.

Finally, the proposal doesn't directly mentions what we should do for tabber images. More specifically, what are we suppose to do with tabbers that have a flashback image? According to Samurai viper's proposal which dealt with tabber images, it states, "Users now have to make a vote about adding, replacing, or removing an image in a tabber." SV's proposal also gives no exceptions to flashback images meaning all images regardless would need a vote. With the passing of LM41's proposal, does it apply to tabbers as well? The only thing the last proposal states is "If we have an image where a character appears in the actual show instead of flashback, that can also be changed without a vote." However, if you take into account that LM41 also stated, "I'm proposing that we add two new exceptions to the rule with the vote for changing infobox images, it's pretty clear he's talking about his previous vote and nothing to do with the tabbers. If that's the case, the proposal just passed contradicts SV's proposal because SV's proposal states you need a vote to replace a tabber with no exceptions while LM41's proposal states you don't need one, but doesn't mention what we do with tabbers.

So here is my solution. First we overturn the exception given to flashback images. Second, if someone wants to change any character infobox image, they should be required to make a proposal so the rest of the community can at least have a say. This also includes infoboxes with no images as well as tabber images. The only exceptions is if the image is low quality. The only difference is the voting time will be reduced from 2 days to 24 hours or less. This should be enough time to where it won't slow down the wiki, but at the same time it should be enough time for users who want to vote. If this proposal were to pass, I plan on making another one to determine the new time limit for image proposals.

Support

(Include mortal and ghost forms for specific characters in infoboxes or not) by Samurai viper[]

Recently, a tabber was added to the Original Master of Amber's infobox just because we did it with Arcturus. Even though we didn't do with Yang and Morro. And that made me wonder, what makes Arcturus and the other Anacondrai generals important enough to have a tabber while Morro and Yang don't? Especially since they are also characters who were turned into ghosts before the events of the series. So, as you can see, this vote is about agreeing if we should have a tabber about mortal and ghost forms for the characters' in the infoboxes, or not.

I'm not including characters such as Cole, Clouse, or Yang's students in this, because unlike Yang or Morro, both their mortal and ghosts forms are present in the show. By that, not one or the other only appears in flashbacks, pictures, etc.

So, if the vote gets supported, then that means we'll be adding a tabber for other characters who were turned into ghosts before the events of the series, such as Yang, Morro, and even the Original Master of Amber. But if the vote gets opposed, then that means we'll be removing the tabber in Arcturus and the other Anacondrai generals' infoboxes, since they are also characters who were also turned into ghosts before the show.

(Decide whether to close discussions) by Printer89[]

If you've been following along, there has been a surge in trolls and vandalism in the discussions. With the writing of this proposal, there have been seven users blocked since last Thursday. The wiki has done its best to stop the vandalism, but due to the lack of moderation tools and the uncertain arrival time of abuse filters, Toa Kopaka Nuva suggested closing the discussions and moving it to an alternative platform until we get abuse filters. That way, the chances of vandalism is severely low and the discussions can continue without the threat of trolls.

Given this could be a long and complicated plan, I think it's best to make separate proposals - one which asks whether the discussions should be closed and another one which asks which alternative platform to use. This proposal will deal with the former. If this proposal were to pass, the proposal which deals with finding an alternative platform will be made. If it doesn't pass, the discussions will stay (for now).

Note if you don't want to use an alternative platform or if you feel like we can deal with the vandalism on this wiki, you should vote oppose since the next proposal (if there is one) will only have support options to determine the alternative platform.

In case your wondering, the other platforms suggested include:

  • Discord
  • Talk pages on this wiki
  • Alternative wiki

(Don't use community logo & name to advertise Pride Month) by Printer89[]

So this last month, an LGBTQ+ logo was uploaded in celebration of Pride Month. This was the second time the wiki took a stance on such an issue. However, I don't think the wiki should be doing this next year.

The first reason we shouldn't do this in the future is because to be honest, very few people actually cared and instead, people cared about the newest season. In the discussions, there were only two posts made in regards to Pride Month and that occurred within the first five days of June. This post was made in the middle of June, but only received five likes and no replies. Truth be told, a post showing Lloyd reaction to eating a pillow mint and a meme regarding Kai's dragon were more popular.

As seen in the wiki's analytics, the most popular search terms were in regards to the season. Terms like "Season 15" and "Ninjago crystalized" along with the ninja's names were the most popular search terms. Any keywords related to Pride Month were not popular search terms during the month of June despite it being Pride Month. Even Sally, a character some people believe to be bisexual and to be the first speaking LGBTQ+ character, did not crack the top ten.

This kinda ties to my second point which is it takes away when an installment is airing. I actually found it very surprising the wiki had a Pride logo although we were in a middle of a season. I understand there haven't been any episodes aired since May 20, but throughout this current hiatus we've been receiving news that this could be the final season (of something) as well as a trailer for the finale which continued to hype up the season. I think we should be doing the same things ourselves by making a Crystalized logo and changing the theme in regards to Crystalized, but instead we kept the pride logo. In some ways we're saying Pride Month is more important than Crystalized.

Thirdly, out of the TV shows out there, Ninjago has the one of the weakest LGBTQ+ representation. As of the making of this proposal, no person who has worked for Ninjago (as well as the movie) is confirmed to be LGBTQ+. In addition, no speaking character is confirmed to be LGBTQ+. As much as people want to speculate that Sally is LGBTQ+ due to having the pride flag and bisexual flag, she could merely have those flags to be in solidarity of those who identify as LGBTQ+, but we don't even know if those flags means the exact same thing here in the real world. For now, people who feel like Sally is bisexual have just as strong as a reasoning to feel that Lloyd is neutrois or Wu is genderfluid. The only things confirmed to be LGBTQ+ related was in Papergirl when the pride sidewalk appeared and two men could be seen kissing.

Fourthly, if we're going to dedicate an entire month to celebrating Pride Month, wouldn't it be fair if we were to celebrate other events like the events I mentioned in my previous proposal? And although Toa got the logo from someone who claimed pride month is "representing all colors (human diversity in terms of religion, gender, sex preferences, ethnicities), and peace and union", I think this line of thought is contrary to what people perceive Pride Month to be. As Ninja72 said, "A cisgender or heterosexual person would not identify with the rainbow flag even if the creator of the flag intended it to be for everyone." I also stated that "most people of different ethnicities/race would likely identify with the country of their origin or the country they currently reside and not necessarily the Pride flag." Even if we were to tell people that Pride Month is representative of every single event Fandom celebrates, I think this undermines the meaning of Pride Month and devalues the month altogether.

I think it's perfectly fine for users within the community celebrate Pride Month by making forums in the discussions or blog post, but as I've said before, I don't think the wiki should display the pride logo and use the community name to advertise Pride Month. If this vote were to pass, the wiki won't be displaying the pride flag as well as using the community name to advertise Pride Month in the future.

Support

(Set Time Limit on Dropping Proposals and add an option to extend a vote) by Toa Kopaka Nuva[]

Recently a proposal was dropped under 24 hours which was quite frankly upsetting to me. Don't get me wrong I agree with the original submitter that subject matter needed more discussion, but it seemed wrong to drop it at that point in time when it had a majority of support. I don't want to make a big deal out of that situation as ultimately the user acted appropriately with what the rules allow and I respect that.

However I do see an issue with the lack of rules we have on drops. Currently the only rule on drops is "If you happen to drop your proposal, you may not create another proposal unless there is more than one spot available.".

My proposal is:

A vote can be dropped if:

At any point in its life it has significantly more opposes than supports or no votes entirely. This will allow the creator to rework the vote without requesting admin approval. Currently this is the most frequent reason for a dropped vote.


At any point in its life and a majority of users have agreed to drop the request.

A vote can not be dropped if:

The vote is in the final day of life and has significantly more support or the vote is near deadlocked.

A vote may be extended if:

If a vote falls bellow the 24 hour cut off for dropping or more discussion is needed prior to the 24 hour cut off, the creator can request for a 24 hour extension. Extension requests take place in the comments and need one voting user to approve. Further extensions must be approved by an administrator.

I'd be willing to discuss these further, but I do feel like they would be beneficial to Ninjago Wiki voting. --Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk) 15:54, 2 July 2022 (UTC)

(Spilt galleries by season onto separate pages) by LuigiMaster41[]

So a few years ago, I made a proposal to have galleries split by season onto separate pages, though ultimately, it was dropped. After being allowed to be brought back by Toa Kopaka Nuva, I wanted to give this proposal another shot, as I feel like the idea wasn't even considered or thought about through enough properly.

So, looking at the Ninja, Wu and Nya's galleries, there are literally a LOT of images onto one page. That's quite problematic as it causes long loading times, especially if it is necessary to edit the whole page. And since we'll being getting more gallery sections for the seasons and filling them up for every episode they appear in, that's going to even further increase the loading times whether you're just viewing the page or editing it.

If you take a look at these examples, the former is split between screenshots, scans, artworks, sprites and models, etc., whilst with the latter, it is split between the seasons and installments, and both include a navigation to each in some format. And with the former example, it even notes down how they were split to reduce loading times.

So I'd suggest that we follow along with those examples. How this will be formatted out, let's give an example with Kai's gallery page. We would only focus on moving the season's galleries to separate pages, whilst leaving minifigures, face prints, official artwork, non-canon installments and games onto the main gallery page.

(Add "Other appearances and mentions" section) by Wikifan988[]

This proposal is based on a previous one by Legoninjagofan600. That vote proposed to remove mentions from character history sections such as Pythor's SoG, SotFS, and MotM, since they are not actually part of the character's personal history, and rather, only things that are said about the character by others.

I agree with this general idea, as I feel it makes the most sense if biography sections are limited to information about the character's life. However, I feel that mentions (and certain types of appearances, which will be specified below) are still deserving of mentions. Previously, I made a few proposals attempting to deal with some of this by creating the "Influence" or "Legacy" sections, and these were passed, but I believe this hasn't made things much better because it's still inconsistent across pages.

So, I propose that we do Legoninjagofan's proposal with the addition of an "Other appearances and mentions" section that would come right after histories/biographies (not just character pages- it could also be on applicable location pages, and so on). The section could be shortened to just "Other appearances" or "Other mentions" depending on the context. These sections would include all "appearances" and mentions that aren't already in the history section: dreams, hallucinations, statues, paintings, etc. That way, there is still a somewhat detailed description of all the character's secondary appearances while letting the history sections remain more focused about a character's personal history.

These sections would be organized the same as history sections usually are, with headings for each episode, only now there wouldn't have to be a note like "(dream)" next to any of them, since it would be specified in the description.

A few notes:

  • There should be some exceptions for mentions that would stay in biographies. This is because certain mentions provide new information about the character even if the character didn't make an official appearance in that installment. For example, information from the first and fourth paragraphs here are from episodes Ray was absent, but they are still kept in the biography.
    • In a similar vein, I believe information about what other characters did immediately following a character's death or disappearance should be included, because it often flows logically from the information about the character's departure and is not too disconnected from the character's own personal history yet. One example is the last paragraph of the same section of Ray's page, which notes that Kai and Nya took over the shop after his disappearance.
  • One thing I'm 100% clear on is the fact that in certain information in Legacy sections would not fit neatly into any specific "Other appearance or mention" so to speak, but are still relevant to the character's posthumous presence or effect on other characters in my opinion. Two examples: Dr. Julien's Legacy, in the first and second-to-last paragraphs about events of Tick Tock and Awakenings respectively; and Cliff Gordon's Legacy, in paragraphs describing events from Misfortune Rising. Could Zane's "protect" quote in Awakenings count as an indirect mention for Dr. Julien? And could Tick Tock and Misfortune Rising be included in the "Other appearances and mentions" sections for those characters despite the fact that other information from those episodes is already in the History section? Let me know what you think.

Let me know if you feel that there's anything else about this that could cause confusion down the line or make things more complicated for readers.

Support

(Disallow users from advertising on other's RoR, EoTM and Votes) by LuigiMaster41[]

Recently, I've noticed that when a user makes a Vote or Request for Rights, and the votes are currently neck and neck, one user will start advertising to other users regarding the vote. However, I want to make the proposal to disallow this entirely for these reasons.

For the Request for Rights (and possibly Editor of the Month), users who are filing a resumé or being nominated respectively are not allowed to advertise to other users. However, we allow voting users to advertise such? I think this is highly unfair if we allow this, because I think it gives way too much power for voting users to advertise in order to potentially lead the voting in their favour, and this also seems extremely biased to do such and just seems plain hurtful if it works out in the other user's favour to collect opposing votes, and also makes the voting system a bit corrupt in that way. Also, my predicament is that they'll ask as many users as they want to in order to get the opposing votes, until the Oppose option is the highest, given the example with Legoninjagofan600's Content Moderator Request for Rights proposal.

I also believe its completely ridiculous to just want to advertise a proposal when it comes to the Votes. Like, if the Support and Oppose options are tied, it is like you want to get the proposal to pass or fail without regard of considering other's actual opinions. Personally, all of the above reasons I stated justifies my point.

So, by making this proposal, we would disallow users to advertise proposals, EoTM and RoR to keep to a balanced, more merciful voting system. Use of the Discord server should also be prohibited too.

Support

  1.   LuigiMaster41   Talk 20:25, 30 July 2022 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. In most cases, there is no way to know for certain if the person who is being asked/notified of the vote will take the same side as the person who is asking them. So by asking another user, users are taking a huge risk. The vote can just as easily end in favour of the opposite side instead of the side that user is on. Like for example, in your infoboxes vote in January, I was the one who asked SoyP777 and NinjaBrix to vote on Discord but they voted for changing the design entirely which caused my side to lose. Even in the rare cases where the user who is asking does know that the user they are asking will take their side (like when I asked Toa to vote on my Skylor infobox image vote in January), voting is for everyone who is eligible, not just everyone who was looking at the votes page or the request page during the voting period. Additionally, users who make Rfrs are allowed to ask other users for their opinion as long as they are not asking them to specifically vote support. There is a difference between "Hey, I made an Rfr, could you please support me?" and "Hey, I made an Rfr, what do you think about it?"Ninja72 (talk) 20:41, 30 July 2022 (UTC)

(In-universe song infobox) by Wikifan988[]

This vote was allowed by Toa Kopaka Nuva to be brought back, with Legoninjagofan600's permission as well.

In the original proposal, I argued that this was unneeded because most in-universe song pages are pretty short, and Quinton1721 also noted that there aren't that many in-universe song articles to begin with. However, I changed my mind and I would argue that even if there aren't that many articles and the pages are not too long, they're still long and significant enough that it would be reasonable to have an infobox.

The infobox would list in-universe singer/songwriter, real-life singer/artist, first appearance, and latest appearance. There could also be a real-life songwriter field if that's known. For pages such as The Weekend Whip and Inner Steel, which are officially released songs that also appear in-universe, both infoboxes could be present, with the in-universe song infobox below the regular song one, and a screenshot from the show used as the image in the in-universe one.

(Deal with the generic/real life food articles) by Samurai viper[]

In the past month, users kept making pages for simple ordinary food. The same thing happened last year with pizza and sandwiches, which got deleted, because they were too generic and not important enough.

Let's say I decided to make a page for simple burgers. Nothing special about them than just being used as ordinary food like french fries and prune juice. But if someone suggests on deleting the article regarding the burgers, I'm afraid I'm gonna have to disagree as long simple articles such as fries, prune juice, and lemonade are still standing. And I won't be the only one who thinks so since we can all agree how we are when it comes to fairness in the main articles and use other users/edits as an excuse. Literally, the reason the pizza article was made was because of the sandwich article, and last week a user got mad that the croissants article got deleted and wanted to get rid of the Rodrigo page (which was created by the user who deleted the croissants page) because of it.

Anyway, I'm recommending getting rid of simple generic food unless they're used for something more than eating and/or recurring in the show, like we're supposed to. Note: Supporting the vote means keeping it, just to clarify.

Used more than just eating (example, weaponry)

Support

  2. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 11:47, 23 September 2022 (UTC)

  1. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 11:47, 23 September 2022 (UTC)

Comments

I think these pages should be deleted, for example the mentioned french fries page has absolutely no meaning, it doesn't even have an image. And even if it is recurring, it still does not mean that it is not useless. At least I think so. Perhaps it could be decided based on whether the food appeared in sets and also whether it was mentioned in the show itself. For example, noodles don't have that much plot relevance, but they appear quite often and are also referenced. As for pages like pancakes or cookies, these should stay as they have a role in the episodes other than being eaten (Aspheera and Wu's competition, Jay and Kai's cookie fight). Also, if it has some specific name, I think it should remain, such as Violet Berry Soup, Moss-milk or Puffy Potsticker. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 11:47, 23 September 2022 (UTC)

You're right about the pancakes and cookies, and remember, this vote is about real life food. It's okay to make pages about food that originated from the show. Samurai viper (talk) 12:44, 23 September 2022 (UTC)

(Prohibit the adding of spoilers in case of release new episodes in another language) by Legoninjagofan600[]

At present, the wiki rule is that if the episode is released in a language other than English, the information about the episode can be added to the pages as long as they are invisible in reading mode. However, for us, editors, it is difficult to avoid spoilers if we see, for example, something like this (image). Although the ordinary reader does not notice it, any editor does. Since several episodes of Crystalized in Chinese were released yesterday, I propose to prohibit adding this information to the pages overall until the episodes are released. I really wouldn't want the key points from the final season to be spoiled that way.

(End the Ninjago Wiki's two chance at applying for staff policy) by FangpyreMoonstone[]

The Ninjago Wiki staff has a rule saying that users can only apply for staff rights twice even if they were accepted. However, They haven't bothered to write it down in the policy. It's only been enforced once, although, the policy has been around for many years. This is extremely strict, isn't official and could easily escalate to deception, harassment and retaliation. This wiki deals with many young users that are teenagers or college students. Any staff team that thinks it's okay to tell a young user that they're not good enough and can never apply for a staff position again in the future is corrupt. This is extremely Bureaucratic and isn't even an official rule. This policy should be 100% removed from the wiki.

  • If this request isn't accepted then it should be officially added but any users with it already effecting such as Icequeen NinjaWarrior should have the sanction 100% removed and they should be allowed to request rights if they would like.

Support

Oppose

  1. The rule has never been "you can apply for staff twice", it is if you are demoted for abuse of power, then you are only given one more chance. If someone has been given a second chance and still has not changed by the time they make it, they are not suitable to be staff and this is final. You need to get over it and let go. Being young is not an excuse. It just means that the users in questions need to learn to take no for an answer because that is one of the most important life lessons people have to learn when they are still growing up.Ninja72 (talk) 22:51, 6 October 2022 (UTC)
  2. I could see adding a time limit/admin vote before an additional request can be made, but removing the rule completely is not the solution. Yes, people can change but if in the past it has been proven they can’t be trusted with the rights it is important to be careful. I’d love to hear a counter proposal to this that offers a drop off period but doesn’t get rid of this restriction.—Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk)
  3. Legoninjagofan600 (talk) 08:02, 9 October 2022 (UTC)

Neutral

Comments

(What should we do with the Weapons of Destruction) by Samurai viper[]

Recently, the individual weapons for the Weapons of Destruction were revealed, as shown in the synopsis of "The Coming of the King" on the LEGO's YouTube channel, the crystallized Scythe of Quakes was actually called the Scythe of Destruction. (Policy for the amount of times users can request staff rights) by FangpyreMoonstone[]

This wiki has an unofficial staff rule claiming that users who were demoted can only reapply once. However, the rule is not official. Since it's not written down it's unprofessional for the community. The rule must be removed from this wikis bureaucratic system. However, some of this wikis staff believe the rule should exist. So the following are possible rules we could include. In all of the following options anyone effected by current sanctions is reset. Whichever one the community approves of will be added to the Ninjago Wik:Policy.

(Allow Leaked Images) by 44NightStalker[]

It's leaked season again and new leaks are coming out. Unfortunetly, this wiki has a policy that users who upload leaks will be blocked. This is okay for dealing with articles but this wiki's got to allow leaks on blog posts and threads.

Support

Oppose

  1. I can’t even allow this if it were to pass. However rather than removing it I’ll write my reasons below. Allowing such content would put us at odds with both LEGO and Fandom. LEGO has contacted Fandom to remove leaks elsewhere on Fandom before. Not to mention, somebody once tried to make a LEGO leaks wiki that was promptly shut down. This vote misses the reason that leaks aren’t allowed which is that LEGO’s legal team doesn’t want them out there. They wouldn't care where on the wiki they are. As such content is basically against Fandom’s terms of use as well. The following is from the Fandom Terms of Use “You also represent and warrant that you own or have the necessary licenses, rights, releases, consents, and permissions to permit the Company to copy, store, publish, display, and distribute your content via the Services, in accordance with the license rules that are applicable to such content (for example, text submissions by you to Fandom communities are subject to the licensing terms set forth at Licensing).” What this means is that when you add content to Fandom you must have the necessary permissions to add it. If something is a leak, the necessary permissions cannot be given as by definition a leak is something that has been unintentionally shared. Feel free to ask any questions, however for the above reasons it cannot be passed. Being at odds with LEGO’s legal team as well as Fandom is a risk we cannot take.—Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk) 13:54, 7 November 2022 (UTC)
  2. There's not really much point anyway of allowing leaked images, if someone wants all the leaks there's tens of social media platforms out there. NinjagoCity17 (talk) 17:54, 8 November 2022 (UTC)
  3. Even if LEGO didn't pay any attention to this site at all, the wiki becoming the go-to place to find the latest Ninjago leaks has too much potential to cause issues. Warptoad (talk) 22:53, 8 November 2022 (UTC)
  4. JN226 (talk)
  5. I know this proposal already will not pass, so I just wanted to share my opposition here, in hopes to persuade this user to not ever allows leaks on this wiki. It's a disregard shown to LEGO and to those who work on this show and has its legal complications.—Preceding unsigned comment added by LuigiMaster41 (talk • contribs)

(Decide how to do appearances when it comes to Groups/Species) by Samurai viper[]

After looking at the appearances of most of the groups' infoboxes, I noticed something odd. How come when a team of six heroes appear, their appearances count not matter what during the time the team was formed. But when a team of six villains appear, appearances only counts if there's only four or all six of them during the council's existence? And also the Ghost Warriors and the Sky Pirates. Morro can count for the Ghost Warriors, Nadakhan can count for the Sky Pirates, but Harumi and Mister F can't count for the Crystal Council? And the council's appearance in "A Sinister Shadow" is considered a mention?

Show/Book/Game appearances[]

So, I have two options on what we should do for appearances when it comes to groups and species. I'm not including families in this, because there doesn't seem to have any problems for families…yet.

  • Option 1: At least one member has to appear, as long as they were an actual member of the group. Like we did for certain articles.
  • Option 2: Three or more members have to be featured for the group's appearances.
Option 1

Set appearances[]

How come set appearances don't count for a council, but it's okay for the ninja? If it was because the members appear in the sets separately, then we might wanna do something with the ninja. Because both the council and the ninja appear in the sets separately in the ones I just listed, and Lloyd and Nya weren't even a ninja at the time.

Ninja
  • 2111 Kai (Kai)
  • 2112 Cole (Cole)
  • 2113 Zane (Zane)
  • 2172 Nya (Nya)
  • 2259 Skull Motorbike (Jay)
  • 9443 Rattlecopter (Lloyd)
Council of the Crystal King
  • 71769 Cole's Dragon Cruiser (Aspheera)
  • 71770 Zane's Golden Dragon Jet (Vangelis)
  • 71772 The Crystal King (Harumi)
  • 71773 Kai's Golden Dragon Raider (Mister F)
  • 71775 Nya's Samurai X MECH (Pythor and the Mechanic)

And it's not just the council. Other groups appear not to have sets they were included in to be included in infoboxes: Serpentine, Stone Army, Nindroid Army, Anacondrai Cultists, Ghost Warriors, Sky Pirates, Yang's students, the Vermillion, the Oni, etc. See what I'm saying? So, I think we should also vote how we should do set appearances when it comes to species and groups as well.

If the voted is the supported, we will include sets for the groups/species' appearances. But we'll place them like we did for certain articles like dragons, Munce, and Merlopians, to be fair. Not individually like we did for the ninja. If it's opposed, then we'll remove them. For all of them. Because again, it is unfair for certain villainous factions not to have their set appearances, but include it for the ninja. (Change Discussions Rule on Religion) by Toa Kopaka Nuva[]

A long time rule has stated to "Avoid religious and/or political discussions unless they are in the context of the Ninjago universe". This rule would allow for discussions of Ninjago religion (Ie: Monks). But not religions as they exist in a real life context. This was done in order to prevent drama and arguments. Recently a group of users has said they believe such topics can be added without leading to these conclusions. I'm willing to give it a chance but want to hear what others have to say.

(Limit the number of staff members per function) by Matt600[]

Due to recent events and the fact that we currently have 6 discussion moderators and others applying for the position, I propose that we limit the number of staff members for a certain position. This is what the number of people for one position would look like:

Bureaucrats 1
Administrators 4
Content moderators 4
Discussions moderators 6 (for now)
Rollbacks 5

I'm not saying it's bad to have a lot of active moderators, but six seems like a lot to me. It's difficult to control and also a bit pointless. However, I don't want to take away anyone's rights, so for now the maximum number would be 6, but later it could be reduced even more.
